issues.quote: She had stopped playing, and we went on with our game.
issues.fact: D2: Madame began to play the piano as I went out, and she stopped when I came back.
issues.misreading: The past-perfect 'had stopped' can be read as the piano ending before Vauthier returned to the salon, possibly while he was still in the hall. The fact is that she stopped at the moment he came back, so the order of the piano stopping and his return is unclear.

issues.quote: The marble mantel clock. It is the one Odile has always kept by the piano.
issues.fact: D3 says only 'the salon clock'. The sheet gives no description of the clock and no location for it.
issues.misreading: Placing the clock by the piano adds a whereabouts. A solver could infer it was within Madame's line of sight or reach while she played, which the sheet does not state.

issues.quote: It stopped with its master. I say that as a friend and not as a physician.
issues.fact: The sheet gives no information about the regulator stopping or about when it stopped.
issues.misreading: A solver could read this as the regulator stopping at the moment of death, and so treat it as a clock reading for the time of death. The sheet supplies no such reading.
